#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Raspberry Pi MCP23017 I2C GPIO Expander – LED & Switch Demo

Hardware:
  • MCP23017 on I2C bus 1 (default address 0x20)
  • LED + current-limiting resistor on GPA0 (bit 0)
  • Switch (active-low) on GPB7 (bit 7) with internal pull-up enabled

The MCP23017 power-on default state has BANK = 0 (IOCON.BANK = 0).
"""

import fcntl
import os
import signal
import sys
import time

# ── Constants ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I2C_BUS = 1
MCP23017_ADDR = 0x20

# MCP23017 register addresses (BANK = 0, default power-on state)
IODIRA = 0x00
IODIRB = 0x01
GPPUA = 0x0C
GPPUB = 0x0D
GPIOA = 0x12
GPIOB = 0x13

LED_BIT = 0      # GPA0
SWITCH_BIT = 7   # GPB7
DEBOUNCE_S = 0.02

# ── Globals for cleanup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
_running = True
_bus = None


def _cleanup():
    """Turn the LED off and close the I2C bus on exit."""
    global _bus
    if _bus is not None:
        try:
            # GPA0 = 0 → LED off
            _write_reg(GPIOA, 0x00)
        except OSError:
            pass
        try:
            _bus.close()
        except OSError:
            pass
        _bus = None


def _signal_handler(signum, frame):
    """SIGINT handler – request graceful shutdown."""
    global _running
    _running = False


def _write_reg(reg, value):
    """Write a single byte to an MCP23017 register; raise on I/O error."""
    if _bus is None:
        raise RuntimeError("I2C bus not initialised")
    msg = bytes([reg, value])
    if fcntl.ioctl(_bus.fileno(), 0x0706, len(msg)) != len(msg):
        raise OSError("ioctl write length mismatch")
    if os.write(_bus.fileno(), msg) != len(msg):
        raise OSError("short write to MCP23017")


def _read_reg(reg):
    """Read a single byte from an MCP23017 register; raise on I/O error."""
    if _bus is None:
        raise RuntimeError("I2C bus not initialised")
    write_msg = bytes([reg])
    if fcntl.ioctl(_bus.fileno(), 0x0706, len(write_msg)) != len(write_msg):
        raise OSError("ioctl write length mismatch")
    if os.write(_bus.fileno(), write_msg) != len(write_msg):
        raise OSError("short write to MCP23017")
    read_msg = bytearray(1)
    if fcntl.ioctl(_bus.fileno(), 0x0707, len(read_msg)) != len(read_msg):
        raise OSError("ioctl read length mismatch")
    if os.read(_bus.fileno(), read_msg) != len(read_msg):
        raise OSError("short read from MCP23017")
    return read_msg[0]


def _init_mcp23017():
    """Configure the MCP23017: GPA0 as output, GPB7 as input with pull-up."""
    # GPA0 output, all other port A pins input
    _write_reg(IODIRA, 0xFF & ~(1 << LED_BIT))
    # All port B pins input
    _write_reg(IODIRB, 0xFF)
    # Enable internal pull-up on GPB7 only
    _write_reg(GPPUB, 1 << SWITCH_BIT)
    # Start with LED off
    _write_reg(GPIOA, 0x00)


def _read_switch():
    """Return True if the switch is pressed (active-low)."""
    port_b = _read_reg(GPIOB)
    return not bool(port_b & (1 << SWITCH_BIT))


def _debounce_read():
    """Debounce the switch: require the same value twice within DEBOUNCE_S."""
    first = _read_switch()
    time.sleep(DEBOUNCE_S)
    second = _read_switch()
    return first if first == second else None


def main():
    global _bus

    # ── Open I2C bus ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        _bus = os.open(f"/dev/i2c-{I2C_BUS}", os.O_RDWR)
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f"Error: cannot open /dev/i2c-{I2C_BUS}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # ── Verify device presence ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        fcntl.ioctl(_bus.fileno(), 0x0706, 1)
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f"Error: no MCP23017 detected at 0x{MCP23017_ADDR:02X} on bus {I2C_BUS}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        _cleanup()
        sys.exit(1)

    # ── Initialise MCP23017 ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        _init_mcp23017()
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f"Error: MCP23017 init failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        _cleanup()
        sys.exit(1)

    # ── Signal handler ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _signal_handler)

    led_state = False
    print("MCP23017 LED/Switch demo running. Press Ctrl+C to exit.")

    # ── Main loop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        while _running:
            switch = _debounce_read()
            if switch is not None:
                if switch != led_state:
                    led_state = switch
                    new_val = 1 if led_state else 0
                    _write_reg(GPIOA, new_val << LED_BIT)
                    print(f"Switch {'PRESSED' if led_state else 'RELEASED'} → LED {'ON' if led_state else 'OFF'}")
            time.sleep(0.01)
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f"I2C error during loop: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
    finally:
        _cleanup()
        print("Program terminated.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import signal

import logging
import requests
from gpiozero import MotionSensor, LED

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PIR_PIN = 17          # BCM 17 – PIR motion sensor OUT pin
LED_PIN = 18          # BCM 18 – LED control pin
SERVER_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:5000/led"
POLL_INTERVAL = 1.0   # seconds between sensor reads

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
)
log = logging.getLogger("motion_monitor")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Globals for cleanup
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_motion: MotionSensor | None = None
_led: LED | None = None
_running = True


def _cleanup() -> None:
    """Release GPIO resources exactly once."""
    global _motion, _led
    if _motion is not None:
        try:
            _motion.close()
        except Exception as exc:                       # pragma: no cover
            log.warning("Error closing MotionSensor: %s", exc)
        _motion = None
    if _led is not None:
        try:
            _led.close()
        except Exception as exc:                       # pragma: no cover
            log.warning("Error closing LED: %s", exc)
        _led = None


def _handle_signal(signum, _frame) -> None:
    """Graceful shutdown on SIGINT / SIGTERM."""
    global _running
    log.info("Received signal %s – shutting down.", signum)
    _running = False


def send_led_state(state: str) -> None:
    """POST the LED state to the server; log and continue on network error."""
    payload = {"led": state}
    try:
        resp = requests.post(SERVER_URL, json=payload, timeout=5)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        log.info("Server acknowledged LED=%s (HTTP %d).", state, resp.status_code)
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
        log.error("Network error while sending LED=%s: %s", state, exc)


def main() -> int:
    global _motion, _led

    # Register signal handlers for clean shutdown
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _handle_signal)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _handle_signal)

    # Initialise GPIO devices
    try:
        _motion = MotionSensor(PIR_PIN, pull_up=False)
        _led = LED(LED_PIN)
    except Exception as exc:
        log.error("Failed to initialise GPIO: %s", exc)
        _cleanup()
        return 1

    log.info("Monitoring PIR on BCM %d; LED on BCM %d; server %s",
             PIR_PIN, LED_PIN, SERVER_URL)

                motion_detected = bool(_motion.motion_detected)
            except Exception as exc:
                log.warning("Sensor read error: %s – retrying next cycle.", exc)
                motion_detected = False

            if motion_detected:
                log.info("Motion detected – sending LED=on")
                send_led_state("on")
            else:
                log.info("No motion – sending LED=off")
                send_led_state("off")

            # Sleep in small increments so signals are caught promptly
            slept = 0.0
            while _running and slept < POLL_INTERVAL:
                time.sleep(0.1)
                slept += 0.1
    finally:
        _cleanup()
        log.info("GPIO resources released. Bye.")

    return 0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Raspberry Pi 3 B+ – Button-controlled LED

Hardware:
  • LED  on GPIO 17 (BCM) with a 330 Ω current-limiting resistor to GND
  • Button on GPIO 2 (BCM) to GND; internal pull-up enabled so the pin
    reads HIGH when open and LOW when pressed.

Behavior:
  • Button press  -> LED on   +  print("Button pressed: LED on")
  • Button release -> LED off  +  print("Button released: LED off")
  • At startup the LED mirrors the button's initial physical state.
  • Clean shutdown on SIGINT / SIGTERM.
"""

import signal
import sys
import atexit

try:
    from gpiozero import Button, LED
    from gpiozero.exc import GPIOZeroError, GPIODeviceError
except ImportError:
    print("Error: gpiozero is not installed. Install with: sudo apt install python3-gpiozero", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


BUTTON_PIN = 2   # BCM 2 (physical pin 3)
LED_PIN = 17     # BCM 17 (physical pin 11)

button = None
led = None


def cleanup() -> None:
    """Release GPIO resources on exit."""
    global button, led
    if led is not None:
        try:
            led.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        led = None
    if button is not None:
        try:
            button.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        button = None


def handle_signal(signum, frame) -> None:
    """Handle SIGINT / SIGTERM for graceful shutdown."""
    print(f"\nReceived signal {signum}, exiting...")
    cleanup()
    sys.exit(0)


def button_pressed() -> None:
    """Callback when the button is pressed (pin pulled LOW)."""
    led.on()
    print("Button pressed: LED on")


def button_released() -> None:
    """Callback when the button is released (pin pulled HIGH)."""
    led.off()
    print("Button released: LED off")


def main() -> None:
    global button, led

    # Register cleanup on normal interpreter exit
    atexit.register(cleanup)

    # Register signal handlers for graceful shutdown
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, handle_signal)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, handle_signal)

    # Initialize LED
    try:
        led = LED(LED_PIN)
    except (GPIOZeroError, GPIODeviceError) as exc:
        print(f"Error: failed to initialize LED on GPIO {LED_PIN}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Error: unexpected failure initializing LED on GPIO {LED_PIN}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Initialize Button with internal pull-up (default for gpiozero.Button)
    # The button is active-low: pressed => pin LOW => when_pressed fires.
    try:
        button = Button(BUTTON_PIN, pull_up=True, bounce_time=0.05)
    except (GPIOZeroError, GPIODeviceError) as exc:
        print(f"Error: failed to initialize button on GPIO {BUTTON_PIN}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        cleanup()
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Error: unexpected failure initializing button on GPIO {BUTTON_PIN}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        cleanup()
        sys.exit(1)

    # Wire event handlers
    button.when_pressed = button_pressed
    button.when_released = button_released

    # Mirror the button's initial physical state so the LED is correct
    # at startup (e.g., if the button is already pressed when the program
    # starts, the LED should be on).
    if button.is_pressed:
        led.on()
        print("Button already pressed at startup: LED on")
    else:
        led.off()
        print("Button not pressed at startup: LED off")

    print("Waiting for button events... (Ctrl+C to exit)")

    # Keep the program alive; gpiozero runs callbacks in a background thread.
    try:
        signal.pause()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        cleanup()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Configuration

SENSOR_PIN = 4                       # BCM GPIO 4 (physical pin 7)
SERVER_ENDPOINT = "http://localhost:5000/sensor"
USERNAME = "pi"
PASSWORD = "raspberry"
POLL_INTERVAL_S = 5

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Logging
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
)
log = logging.getLogger("sensor_monitor")

# Globals for cleanup
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_sensor: DigitalInputDevice | None = None
_running = True


def _cleanup() -> None:
    """Release GPIO resources exactly once."""
    global _sensor
    if _sensor is not None:
        try:
            _sensor.close()
        except Exception as exc:                       # noqa: BLE001
            log.warning("Error closing sensor: %s", exc)
        _sensor = None


def _handle_signal(signum, _frame) -> None:
    """Graceful shutdown on SIGINT / SIGTERM."""
    global _running
    log.info("Received signal %s – shutting down.", signum)
    _running = False

    global _sensor
    if _sensor is None:
        return None
    try:
        return int(_sensor.value)
    except Exception as exc:                           # noqa: BLE001
        log.error("Sensor read failed: %s", exc)
        return None

    payload = {"sensor": "digital_input", "value": value}

            json=payload,
            auth=HTTPBasicAuth(USERNAME, PASSWORD),
            timeout=10,
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
        log.info("Submitted: %s  (HTTP %s)", payload, resp.status_code)
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
        log.error("Submission failed: %s", exc)


def main() -> int:
    global _sensor

    # Register signal handlers for clean shutdown
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _handle_signal)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _handle_signal)

    # Initialize the digital input with pull_up disabled (floating input)
    try:
        _sensor = DigitalInputDevice(SENSOR_PIN, pull_up=False)
        log.info("GPIO %d initialized as floating input.", SENSOR_PIN)
    except Exception as exc:                           # noqa: BLE001
        log.error("Failed to initialize GPIO %d: %s", SENSOR_PIN, exc)
        return 1

    try:

            if value is not None:
                _submit(value)

            slept = 0.0
            while _running and slept < POLL_INTERVAL_S:

                slept += 0.2
    finally:
        _cleanup()
        log.info("GPIO cleanup completed. Exiting.")
    return 0

import RPi.GPIO as GPIO
import time
import sys

# Configuration
PIR_PIN = 4          # BCM GPIO pin connected to the PIR sensor OUT line
MONITOR_SECONDS = 20 # Duration of the monitoring window
DEBOUNCE_SECONDS = 0.5 # Minimum time between accepted state changes


def setup_pir_sensor(pin):
    """Configure the PIR sensor pin as an input with a pull-down resistor.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If GPIO setup fails (e.g., pin invalid or not accessible).
    """
    try:
        GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BCM)
        GPIO.setup(pin, GPIO.IN, pull_up_down=GPIO.PUD_DOWN)
    except Exception as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to initialize GPIO pin {pin}: {e}")


def read_pir_state(pin):
    """Read the current digital state of the PIR sensor.

    Returns:
        int: 1 if motion detected (HIGH), 0 otherwise (LOW).
    """
    return GPIO.input(pin)


def monitor_motion(pin, duration):
    """Monitor the PIR sensor for motion events over a fixed duration.

    Args:
        pin: BCM GPIO pin number connected to the PIR sensor.
        duration: Monitoring window in seconds.

    Returns:
        int: Total number of motion events detected.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If GPIO setup fails.
    """
    setup_pir_sensor(pin)

    motion_events = 0
    last_state = read_pir_state(pin)
    last_change_time = time.monotonic()

    print("Monitoring for motion...")

    try:
        while time.monotonic() - last_change_time < duration:
            current_state = read_pir_state(pin)
            current_time = time.monotonic()

            # Detect a rising edge (LOW -> HIGH) with debounce
            if current_state == 1 and last_state == 0:
                if current_time - last_change_time >= DEBOUNCE_SECONDS:
                    motion_events += 1
                    print("Motion detected!")
                    last_change_time = current_time

            last_state = current_state
            time.sleep(0.05)  # Light sleep to reduce CPU usage

    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nMonitoring interrupted by user.")
        raise

    return motion_events


def main():
    """Entry point: run the motion monitoring and report results."""
    try:
        total = monitor_motion(PIR_PIN, MONITOR_SECONDS)
        print(f"\nMonitoring complete. Total motion events: {total}")
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nProgram stopped by user.")
        sys.exit(0)
    finally:
        GPIO.cleanup()
        print("GPIO cleanup completed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import signal
import time
from collections import deque
from typing import Optional

import numpy as np
import sounddevice as sd
import tflite_runtime.interpreter as tflite

try:
    from gpiozero import LED
except ImportError:
    LED = None

CONFIG_FILE = "config.json"
DEFAULT_CONFIG = {
    "sampling_rate": 16000,
    "sensitivity": 0.5,
    "keywords": ["hello", "help"],
    "sentiment_thresholds": {"positive": 0.7, "negative": -0.7},
    "led_pin": 17,
    "heartbeat_interval": 60,
    "config_check_interval": 300,
    "resource_log_interval": 60,
    "audio_duration": 1.0,
    "audio_overlap": 0.5,
    "model_path": "model.tflite",
    "cloud_endpoint": None,
    "cloud_interval": 10,
    "cloud_batch_size": 10,
}

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s",
    handlers=[logging.StreamHandler()],
)


class KeywordSpottingSystem:
    def __init__(self, config_file: str = CONFIG_FILE):
        self.config_file = config_file
        self.config: dict = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()
        self.load_config()
        self.running = True
        self.heartbeat_interval = self.config["heartbeat_interval"]
        self.config_check_interval = self.config["config_check_interval"]
        self.resource_log_interval = self.config["resource_log_interval"]
        self.cloud_endpoint = self.config["cloud_endpoint"]
        self.cloud_interval = self.config["cloud_interval"]
        self.cloud_batch_size = self.config["cloud_batch_size"]
        self.cloud_queue: deque = deque()
        self.cloud_task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None
        self.led: Optional[object] = None
        self.interpreter: Optional[tflite.Interpreter] = None
        self.input_details: Optional[list] = None
        self.output_details: Optional[list] = None
        self.sentiment_history: deque = deque(maxlen=10)
        self.last_heartbeat = time.time()
        self.last_config_check = time.time()
        self.last_resource_log = time.time()
        self._shutdown_event = asyncio.Event()

    def load_config(self) -> None:
        try:
            with open(self.config_file, "r") as f:
                loaded = json.load(f)
            self.config.update(loaded)
            logging.info("Configuration loaded successfully.")
        except FileNotFoundError:
            logging.warning("Configuration file not found. Using default settings.")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            logging.error("Invalid JSON in configuration file. Using default settings.")
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error loading configuration: {e}. Using default settings.")

    def initialize_led(self) -> None:
        if LED is not None and self.config.get("led_pin") is not None:
            try:
                self.led = LED(self.config["led_pin"])
                logging.info(f"LED initialized on GPIO {self.config['led_pin']}.")
            except Exception as e:
                logging.error(f"Failed to initialize LED on GPIO {self.config['led_pin']}: {e}")
                self.led = None
        else:
            logging.info("LED initialization skipped (gpiozero not installed or pin not configured).")

    def initialize_tflite(self) -> None:
        model_path = self.config.get("model_path")
        if not model_path or not os.path.exists(model_path):
            logging.warning("TFLite model file not found. Keyword spotting disabled.")
            return
        try:
            self.interpreter = tflite.Interpreter(model_path=model_path)
            self.interpreter.allocate_tensors()
            self.input_details = self.interpreter.get_input_details()
            self.output_details = self.interpreter.get_output_details()
            logging.info("TFLite interpreter initialized successfully.")
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Failed to initialize TFLite interpreter: {e}")
            self.interpreter = None
            self.input_details = None
            self.output_details = None

    def signal_handler(self, signum, frame) -> None:
        logging.info(f"Signal {signum} received. Shutting down...")
        self.running = False
        self._shutdown_event.set()

    def voice_activity_detection(self, audio_data: np.ndarray, sensitivity: float) -> bool:
        rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(audio_data ** 2))
        threshold = sensitivity * 0.01
        return rms > threshold

    def preprocess_audio(self, audio_data: np.ndarray) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
        if self.interpreter is None:
            return None
        try:
            input_shape = self.input_details[0]["shape"]
            audio_data = audio_data.astype(np.float32)
            audio_data = (audio_data - np.mean(audio_data)) / (np.std(audio_data) + 1e-6)
            audio_data = np.pad(audio_data, (0, max(0, input_shape[1] - len(audio_data))), "constant")
            audio_data = audio_data[: input_shape[1]]
            audio_data = np.expand_dims(audio_data, axis=0)
            return audio_data
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error preprocessing audio: {e}")
            return None

    def run_inference(self, audio_data: np.ndarray) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
        if self.interpreter is None:
            return None
        try:
            self.interpreter.set_tensor(self.input_details[0]["index"], audio_data)
            self.interpreter.invoke()
            output_data = self.interpreter.get_tensor(self.output_details[0]["index"])
            return output_data
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error running inference: {e}")
            return None

    def postprocess_output(self, output_data: np.ndarray, keywords: list) -> Optional[str]:
        try:
            predicted_index = int(np.argmax(output_data[0]))
            if predicted_index < len(keywords):
                return keywords[predicted_index]
            return None
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error postprocessing output: {e}")
            return None

    def analyze_sentiment(self, audio_data: np.ndarray) -> float:
        try:
            sentiment_score = float(np.mean(audio_data))
            self.sentiment_history.append(sentiment_score)
            return sentiment_score
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error analyzing sentiment: {e}")
            return 0.0

    def check_sentiment_thresholds(self, sentiment_score: float) -> None:
        thresholds = self.config.get("sentiment_thresholds", {})
        positive_threshold = thresholds.get("positive", 0.7)
        negative_threshold = thresholds.get("negative", -0.7)
        if sentiment_score > positive_threshold:
            logging.warning("Positive sentiment threshold exceeded!")
            self.trigger_alert("Positive sentiment detected!")
        elif sentiment_score < negative_threshold:
            logging.warning("Negative sentiment threshold exceeded!")
            self.trigger_alert("Negative sentiment detected!")

    def trigger_alert(self, message: str) -> None:
        logging.warning(f"ALERT: {message}")
        if self.led is not None:
            try:
                self.led.on()
                time.sleep(1)
                self.led.off()
            except Exception as e:
                logging.error(f"Failed to control LED: {e}")

    def send_cloud_alert(self, message: str) -> None:
        if not self.cloud_endpoint:
            return
        try:
            import requests
            payload = {"timestamp": time.time(), "message": message}
            response = requests.post(self.cloud_endpoint, json=payload, timeout=5)
            response.raise_for_status()
            logging.info(f"Cloud alert sent successfully. Status code: {response.status_code}")
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
            logging.error(f"Failed to send cloud alert: {e}")

    async def capture_audio(self) -> None:
        sampling_rate = self.config["sampling_rate"]
        audio_duration = self.config["audio_duration"]
        audio_overlap = self.config["audio_overlap"]
        sensitivity = self.config["sensitivity"]
        keywords = self.config["keywords"]
        sentiment_thresholds = self.config.get("sentiment_thresholds", {})
        positive_threshold = sentiment_thresholds.get("positive", 0.7)
        negative_threshold = sentiment_thresholds.get("negative", -0.7)

        chunk_size = int(sampling_rate * audio_duration)
        overlap_size = int(sampling_rate * audio_overlap)

        while self.running:
            try:
                audio_data = sd.rec(
                    chunk_size,
                    samplerate=sampling_rate,
                    channels=1,
                    dtype="float32",
                    blocksize=chunk_size,
                )
                sd.wait()

                if not self.voice_activity_detection(audio_data, sensitivity):
                    continue

                preprocessed_audio = self.preprocess_audio(audio_data)
                if preprocessed_audio is not None:
                    output_data = self.run_inference(preprocessed_audio)
                    if output_data is not None:
                        keyword = self.postprocess_output(output_data, keywords)
                        if keyword:
                            logging.info(f"Keyword detected: {keyword}")
                            self.trigger_alert(f"Keyword detected: {keyword}")
                            self.send_cloud_alert(f"Keyword detected: {keyword}")

                sentiment_score = self.analyze_sentiment(audio_data)
                self.check_sentiment_thresholds(sentiment_score)

                if self.cloud_endpoint:
                    self.cloud_queue.append({"timestamp": time.time(), "message": f"Sentiment: {sentiment_score}"})
                    if len(self.cloud_queue) >= self.cloud_batch_size:
                        await self.send_cloud_data()

                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)

            except sd.PortAudioError as e:
                logging.error(f"Audio device error: {e}")
                await asyncio.sleep(1)
            except Exception as e:
                logging.error(f"Error capturing audio: {e}")
                await asyncio.sleep(1)

    async def send_cloud_data(self) -> None:
        if not self.cloud_queue:
            return
        try:
            import requests
            payload = list(self.cloud_queue)
            response = requests.post(self.cloud_endpoint, json=payload, timeout=5)
            response.raise_for_status()
            logging.info(f"Cloud data sent successfully. Status code: {response.status_code}")
            self.cloud_queue.clear()
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
            logging.error(f"Failed to send cloud data: {e}")

    async def cloud_task_loop(self) -> None:
        while self.running:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.cloud_interval)
            await self.send_cloud_data()

    async def heartbeat_task(self) -> None:
        while self.running:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.heartbeat_interval)
            if time.time() - self.last_heartbeat > self.heartbeat_interval:
                logging.warning("Heartbeat lost!")
                self.trigger_alert("Heartbeat lost!")
            self.last_heartbeat = time.time()

    async def config_check_task(self) -> None:
        while self.running:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.config_check_interval)
            if time.time() - self.last_config_check > self.config_check_interval:
                logging.info("Checking for configuration updates...")
                self.load_config()
                self.initialize_led()
                self.initialize_tflite()
                self.last_config_check = time.time()

    async def resource_log_task(self) -> None:
        while self.running:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.resource_log_interval)
            if time.time() - self.last_resource_log > self.resource_log_interval:
                try:
                    import psutil
                    cpu_usage = psutil.cpu_percent(interval=None)
                    memory_usage = psutil.virtual_memory().percent

try:

}

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s",
    handlers=[logging.StreamHandler()],
)


class KeywordSpottingSystem:
    def __init__(self, config_file: str = CONFIG_FILE):
        self.config_file = config_file
        self.config: dict = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()
        self.load_config()
        self.running = True
        self.heartbeat_interval = self.config["heartbeat_interval"]
        self.config_check_interval = self.config["config_check_interval"]
        self.resource_log_interval = self.config["resource_log_interval"]
        self.cloud_endpoint = self.config["cloud_endpoint"]
        self.cloud_interval = self.config["cloud_interval"]
        self.cloud_batch_size = self.config["cloud_batch_size"]
        self.cloud_queue: deque = deque()
        self.cloud_task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None
        self.led: Optional[object] = None
        self.interpreter: Optional[tflite.Interpreter] = None
        self.input_details: Optional[list] = None
        self.output_details: Optional[list] = None
        self.sentiment_history: deque = deque(maxlen=10)
        self.last_heartbeat = time.time()
        self.last_config_check = time.time()
        self.last_resource_log = time.time()
        self._shutdown_event = asyncio.Event()

    def load_config(self) -> None:
        try:
            with open(self.config_file, "r") as f:
                loaded = json.load(f)
            self.config.update(loaded)
            logging.info("Configuration loaded successfully.")
        except FileNotFoundError:
            logging.warning("Configuration file not found. Using default settings.")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            logging.error("Invalid JSON in configuration file. Using default settings.")
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error loading configuration: {e}. Using default settings.")

    def initialize_led(self) -> None:
        if LED is not None and self.config.get("led_pin") is not None:
            try:
                self.led = LED(self.config["led_pin"])
                logging.info(f"LED initialized on GPIO {self.config['led_pin']}.")
            except Exception as e:
                logging.error(f"Failed to initialize LED on GPIO {self.config['led_pin']}: {e}")
                self.led = None
        else:
            logging.info("LED initialization skipped (gpiozero not installed or pin not configured).")

    def initialize_tflite(self) -> None:
        model_path = self.config.get("model_path")
        if not model_path or not os.path.exists(model_path):
            logging.warning("TFLite model file not found. Keyword spotting disabled.")
            return
        try:
            self.interpreter = tflite.Interpreter(model_path=model_path)
            self.interpreter.allocate_tensors()
            self.input_details = self.interpreter.get_input_details()
            self.output_details = self.interpreter.get_output_details()
            logging.info("TFLite interpreter initialized successfully.")
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Failed to initialize TFLite interpreter: {e}")
            self.interpreter = None
            self.input_details = None
            self.output_details = None

    def signal_handler(self, signum, frame) -> None:
        logging.info(f"Signal {signum} received. Shutting down...")
        self.running = False
        self._shutdown_event.set()

    def voice_activity_detection(self, audio_data: np.ndarray, sensitivity: float) -> bool:
        rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(audio_data ** 2))
        threshold = sensitivity * 0.01
        return rms > threshold

    def preprocess_audio(self, audio_data: np.ndarray) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
        if self.interpreter is None:
            return None
        try:
            input_shape = self.input_details[0]["shape"]
            audio_data = audio_data.astype(np.float32)
            audio_data = (audio_data - np.mean(audio_data)) / (np.std(audio_data) + 1e-6)
            audio_data = np.pad(audio_data, (0, max(0, input_shape[1] - len(audio_data))), "constant")
            audio_data = audio_data[: input_shape[1]]
            audio_data = np.expand_dims(audio_data, axis=0)
            return audio_data
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error preprocessing audio: {e}")
            return None

    def run_inference(self, audio_data: np.ndarray) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
        if self.interpreter is None:
            return None
        try:
            self.interpreter.set_tensor(self.input_details[0]["index"], audio_data)
            self.interpreter.invoke()
            output_data = self.interpreter.get_tensor(self.output_details[0]["index"])
            return output_data
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error running inference: {e}")
            return None

    def postprocess_output(self, output_data: np.ndarray, keywords: list) -> Optional[str]:
        try:
            predicted_index = int(np.argmax(output_data[0]))
            if predicted_index < len(keywords):
                return keywords[predicted_index]
            return None
        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error postprocessing output: {e}")
            return None

        try:

            self.sentiment_history.append(sentiment_score)

        except Exception as e:
            logging.error(f"Error analyzing sentiment: {e}")
            return 0.0

        thresholds = self.config.get("sentiment_thresholds", {})
        positive_threshold = thresholds.get("positive", 0.7)
        negative_threshold = thresholds.get("negative", -0.7)
        if sentiment_score > positive_threshold:
            logging.warning("Positive sentiment threshold exceeded!")
            self.trigger_alert("Positive sentiment detected!")
        elif sentiment_score < negative_threshold:
            logging.warning("Negative sentiment threshold exceeded!")
            self.trigger_alert("Negative sentiment detected!")

    def trigger_alert(self, message: str) -> None:

        try:

        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
            logging.error(f"Failed to send cloud alert: {e}")

    async def capture_audio(self) -> None:
        sampling_rate = self.config["sampling_rate"]
        audio_duration = self.config["audio_duration"]
        audio_overlap = self.config["audio_overlap"]
        sensitivity = self.config["sensitivity"]
        keywords = self.config["keywords"]
        sentiment_thresholds = self.config.get("sentiment_thresholds", {})
        positive_threshold = sentiment_thresholds.get("positive", 0.7)
        negative_threshold = sentiment_thresholds.get("negative", -0.7)

        chunk_size = int(sampling_rate * audio_duration)
        overlap_size = int(sampling_rate * audio_overlap)

        while self.running:
            try:
                audio_data = sd.rec(
                    chunk_size,
                    samplerate=sampling_rate,
                    channels=1,
                    dtype="float32",
                    blocksize=chunk_size,
                )
                sd.wait()

                if not self.voice_activity_detection(audio_data, sensitivity):
                    continue

                preprocessed_audio = self.preprocess_audio(audio_data)
                if preprocessed_audio is not None:
                    output_data = self.run_inference(preprocessed_audio)
                    if output_data is not None:
                        keyword = self.postprocess_output(output_data, keywords)
                        if keyword:
                            logging.info(f"Keyword detected: {keyword}")
                            self.trigger_alert(f"Keyword detected: {keyword}")
                            self.send_cloud_alert(f"Keyword detected: {keyword}")

                sentiment_score = self.analyze_sentiment(audio_data)
                self.check_sentiment_thresholds(sentiment_score)

                if self.cloud_endpoint:
                    self.cloud_queue.append({"timestamp": time.time(), "message": f"Sentiment: {sentiment_score}"})
                    if len(self.cloud_queue) >= self.cloud_batch_size:
                        await self.send_cloud_data()

                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)

            except sd.PortAudioError as e:
                logging.error(f"Audio device error: {e}")
                await asyncio.sleep(1)
            except Exception as e:
                logging.error(f"Error capturing audio: {e}")
                await asyncio.sleep(1)

    async def send_cloud_data(self) -> None:
        if not self.cloud_queue:
            return
        try:
            import requests
            payload = list(self.cloud_queue)
            response = requests.post(self.cloud_endpoint, json=payload, timeout=5)
            response.raise_for_status()
            logging.info(f"Cloud data sent successfully. Status code: {response.status_code}")
            self.cloud_queue.clear()
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
            logging.error(f"Failed to send cloud data: {e}")

    async def cloud_task_loop(self) -> None:
        while self.running:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.cloud_interval)
            await self.send_cloud_data()

    async def heartbeat_task(self) -> None:
        while self.running:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.heartbeat_interval)
            if time.time() - self.last_heartbeat > self.heartbeat_interval:
                logging.warning("Heartbeat lost!")
                self.trigger_alert("Heartbeat lost!")
            self.last_heartbeat = time.time()

    async def config_check_task(self) -> None:
        while self.running:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.config_check_interval)
            if time.time() - self.last_config_check > self.config_check_interval:
                logging.info("Checking for configuration updates...")
                self.load_config()
                self.initialize_led()
                self.initialize_tflite()
                self.last_config_check = time.time()

    async def resource_log_task(self) -> None:
        while self.running:
            await asyncio.sleep(self.resource_log_interval)
            if time.time() - self.last_resource_log > self.resource_log_interval:
                try:
                    import psutil
                    cpu_usage = psutil.cpu_percent(interval=None)
                    memory_usage = psutil.virtual_memory().percent
                    logging.info(f"CPU Usage: {cpu_usage}%, Memory Usage: {memory_usage}%")
                except Exception as e:
                    logging.error(f"Error logging resource usage: {e}")
                self.last_resource_log = time.time()

    async def run(self) -> None:
        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, self.signal_handler)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, self.signal_handler)

        self.initialize_led()
        self.initialize_tflite()

        self.cloud_task = asyncio.create_task(self.cloud_task_loop())
        asyncio.create_task(self.heartbeat_task())
        asyncio.create_task(self.config_check_task())
        asyncio.create_task(self.resource_log_task())

        await self.capture_audio()

        if self.cloud_task:
            self.cloud_task.cancel()
        self._shutdown_event.set()
        logging.info("System shutdown complete.")

    await system.run()

TSL2561_REGISTER_CONTROL = 0x00
TSL2561_REGISTER_TIMING = 0x01
TSL2561_REGISTER_DATA0LOW = 0x0C
TSL2561_REGISTER_DATA1LOW = 0x0E
TSL2561_REGISTER_CHAN0_LOW = 0x0C
TSL2561_REGISTER_CHAN1_LOW = 0x0E
TSL2561_REGISTER_CONTROL_POWER_ON = 0x03
TSL2561_REGISTER_TIMING_13MS = 0x00
LED_GPIO_PIN = 18

MAX_LUX = 1000.0

    global running
    running = False
    logger.info("Shutdown signal received. Cleaning up...")

    except Exception as e:

        return None

        bus.write_byte_data(TSL2561_ADDR, TSL2561_COMMAND_BIT | TSL2561_REGISTER_CONTROL, TSL2561_REGISTER_CONTROL_POWER_ON)
        time.sleep(0.01)  # Wait for power-on to settle
        # Set timing to 13ms integration (max gain)
        bus.write_byte_data(TSL2561_ADDR, TSL2561_COMMAND_BIT | TSL2561_REGISTER_TIMING, TSL2561_REGISTER_TIMING_13MS)
        time.sleep(0.01)
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Failed to initialize TSL2561 light sensor: {e}")
        return False

def read_light_level(bus):
    try:
        # Read channel 0 (visible + infrared) and channel 1 (infrared)
        data0 = bus.read_i2c_block_data(TSL2561_ADDR, TSL2561_COMMAND_BIT | TSL2561_REGISTER_CHAN0_LOW, 2)
        data1 = bus.read_i2c_block_data(TSL2561_ADDR, TSL2561_COMMAND_BIT | TSL2561_REGISTER_CHAN1_LOW, 2)
        
        channel0 = data0[1] * 256 + data0[0]
        channel1 = data1[1] * 256 + data1[0]

        if channel0 == 0:
            return 0.0
        ratio = channel1 / channel0
        if 0 < ratio <= 0.52:

        elif ratio <= 0.80:
            lux = 0.0157 * channel0 - 0.0180 * channel1
        elif ratio <= 1.3:
            lux = 0.00338 * channel0 - 0.00260 * channel1
        else:
            lux = 0.0
        
        return max(0.0, lux)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Error reading light sensor: {e}")
        return None

    try:
        normalized = min(lux / max_lux, 1.0)
        return normalized * 100
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Error mapping lux to brightness: {e}")
        return 0

    global running
    
    # Register signal handler for graceful shutdown
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal_handler)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal_handler)
    
    # Initialize I2C bus
    bus = initialize_i2c_bus()

        sys.exit(1)
    
    last_brightness = 0.0

        while running:
            lux = read_light_level(bus)
            
            if lux is not None:
                brightness = map_lux_to_brightness(lux)
                last_brightness = brightness
                led.value = brightness / 100.0
                logger.info(f"Lux: {lux:.2f}, Brightness: {brightness:.2f}%")
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Sensor read failed. Retaining previous brightness: {last_brightness:.2f}%")
            
            # Sleep for 1 second, checking running flag periodically for responsive shutdown
            for _ in range(10):
                if not running:
                    break
                time.sleep(0.1)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Unexpected error in main loop: {e}")
    finally:
        # Clean up resources
        led.close()
        bus.close()
        logger.info("Resources cleaned up. Exiting.")

    main()

import RPi.GPIO as GPIO
import time
import sys

# GPIO pins (BCM numbering) for the two TCRT5000 line sensors
LEFT_SENSOR_PIN = 5
RIGHT_SENSOR_PIN = 6

# Sampling parameters
SAMPLE_INTERVAL = 0.5   # seconds between readings
NUM_SAMPLES = 10        # total readings to take


def setup_gpio():
    """Configure the GPIO pins for the line sensors as inputs with pull-down resistors."""
    try:
        GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BCM)
        GPIO.setup(LEFT_SENSOR_PIN, GPIO.IN, pull_up_down=GPIO.PUD_DOWN)
        GPIO.setup(RIGHT_SENSOR_PIN, GPIO.IN, pull_up_down=GPIO.PUD_DOWN)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error setting up GPIO: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


def read_line_sensors():
    """
    Read the two line sensors and return their raw values.
    A reading of 0 means the sensor sees a black line (object present).
    A reading of 1 means the sensor sees a white surface (no object).
    """
    try:
        left_value = GPIO.input(LEFT_SENSOR_PIN)
        right_value = GPIO.input(RIGHT_SENSOR_PIN)
        return left_value, right_value
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error reading sensors: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return None, None


def determine_direction(left_value, right_value):
    """
    Determine the steering direction based on the sensor readings.
    Returns one of: 'forward', 'turn_left', 'turn_right', 'search'.
    """
    if left_value == 0 and right_value == 0:
        return "forward"
    elif left_value == 1 and right_value == 0:
        return "turn_left"
    elif left_value == 0 and right_value == 1:
        return "turn_right"
    else:
        return "search"


def main():
    """Main loop: sample the line sensors and print the navigation status."""
    setup_gpio()
    try:
        for sample_index in range(NUM_SAMPLES):
            left_value, right_value = read_line_sensors()
            if left_value is None or right_value is None:
                print("Sensor read failed; skipping sample.")
                time.sleep(SAMPLE_INTERVAL)
                continue

            direction = determine_direction(left_value, right_value)
            print(f"Sample {sample_index + 1}: Left={left_value}, Right={right_value} -> {direction}")
            time.sleep(SAMPLE_INTERVAL)

    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\nProgram stopped by user.")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Unexpected error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    finally:
        GPIO.cleanup()
        print("GPIO cleanup completed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Tuple

import spidev
from gpiozero import OutputDevice

from lib_tft144 import TFT144

# Color constants (RGB565)
BLACK = 0x0000
BLUE = 0x001F
RED = 0xF800
GREEN = 0x07E0
PINK = 0xF81F
LIGHTBLUE = 0x07FF
LIGHTGREEN = 0x87F0
YELLOW = 0xFFE0
MAGENTA = 0xF81F
CYAN = 0x07FF

COLORS = [BLUE, RED, GREEN, PINK, LIGHTBLUE, LIGHTGREEN, YELLOW, MAGENTA, CYAN]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TFT144Config:
    """Configuration for the TFT144 display."""
    spi_bus: int = 0
    spi_device: int = 0
    dc_pin: int = 22
    reset_pin: int = 18
    led_pin: int = 23
    orientation: int = 1  # 1 = 90 degrees

class TFTDisplayManager:
    """Manages the TFT144 display and its resources."""

    def __init__(self, config: TFT144Config):
        self.config = config
        self.spi = None
        self.led = None
        self.dc = None
        self.reset = None
        self.tft = None
        self._running = True

    def _setup_gpio(self) -> None:
        """Sets up the GPIO pins for the display."""
        try:
            self.led = OutputDevice(self.config.led_pin)
            self.dc = OutputDevice(self.config.dc_pin)
            self.reset = OutputDevice(self.config.reset_pin)
        except Exception as e:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to initialize GPIO pins: {e}") from e

    def _setup_spi(self) -> None:
        """Sets up the SPI interface."""
        try:
            self.spi = spidev.SpiDev()
            self.spi.open(self.config.spi_bus, self.config.spi_device)
            self.spi.max_speed_hz = 32000000
            self.spi.mode = 0
        except Exception as e:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to initialize SPI (bus {self.config.spi_bus}, device {self.config.spi_device}): {e}") from e

    def initialize(self) -> None:
        """Initializes the TFT144 display."""
        self._setup_gpio()
        self._setup_spi()
        self.tft = TFT144(self.spi, self.dc, self.reset, self.led, self.config.orientation)

    def cleanup(self) -> None:
        """Releases all resources."""
        if self.tft is not None:
            try:
                self.tft.clear_display(BLACK)
            except Exception:
                pass
        if self.led is not None:
            self.led.close()
        if self.dc is not None:
            self.dc.close()
        if self.reset is not None:
            self.reset.close()
        if self.spi is not None:
            self.spi.close()

    def _signal_handler(self, signum, frame) -> None:
        """Handles SIGINT and SIGTERM for graceful shutdown."""
        print(f"\nReceived signal {signum}, shutting down...")
        self._running = False

    def run(self) -> None:
        """Runs the display loop."""
        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, self._signal_handler)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, self._signal_handler)

        try:
            self.initialize()
            print("TFT144 initialized successfully. Starting color cycle...")

            while self._running:
                for color in COLORS:
                    if not self._running:
                        break
                    try:
                        self.tft.clear_display(color)
                        self.tft.put_string("Hello", 0, 0, WHITE, BLACK)
                        time.sleep(1)
                        self.tft.put_string("Hello", 0, 0, WHITE, color)
                        time.sleep(2)
                    except Exception as e:
                        print(f"Error during display update: {e}")
                        time.sleep(0.1)

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Initialization or runtime error: {e}")
        finally:
            self.cleanup()
            print("Resources released. Exiting.")

    config = TFT144Config()
    manager = TFTDisplayManager(config)
    manager.run()

RST_PIN = 18
DC_PIN = 22
LED_PIN = 23

# ---- ST7735S constants ----
ST7735_TFTWIDTH = 128
ST7735_TFTHEIGHT = 128
ST7735_NOP = 0x00
ST7735_SWRESET = 0x01
ST7735_SLPOUT = 0x11
ST7735_DISPON = 0x29
ST7735_CASET = 0x2A
ST7735_RASET = 0x2B
ST7735_RAMWR = 0x2C
ST7735_MADCTL = 0x36
ST7735_COLMOD = 0x3A

# ---- Colors (RGB565) ----
BLACK = 0x0000
WHITE = 0xFFFF
RED = 0xF800
GREEN = 0x07E0
BLUE = 0x001F

# ---- Globals for cleanup ----
_spi = None
_running = True


def _cleanup():
    """Release GPIO and SPI resources."""

        try:
            _spi.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        _spi = None
    try:
        GPIO.cleanup()
    except Exception:
        pass


def _signal_handler(signum, frame):
    """Handle SIGINT / SIGTERM for graceful shutdown."""

        self.dc = dc
        self.rst = rst
        self.led = led
        self.width = ST7735_TFTWIDTH
        self.height = ST7735_TFTHEIGHT
        self._init_gpio()
        self._init_display(is_red_board)

        GPIO.setmode(GPIO.BCM)

        GPIO.setup(self.rst, GPIO.OUT)
        GPIO.setup(self.led, GPIO.OUT)
        GPIO.output(self.led, GPIO.HIGH)  # backlight on

        # Hardware reset
        GPIO.output(self.rst, GPIO.HIGH)
        time.sleep(0.01)
        GPIO.output(self.rst, GPIO.LOW)
        time.sleep(0.01)
        GPIO.output(self.rst, GPIO.HIGH)
        time.sleep(0.15)

        # Software reset
        self._write_cmd(ST7735_SWRESET)
        time.sleep(0.15)

        # Out of sleep mode
        self._write_cmd(ST7735_SLPOUT)
        time.sleep(0.5)

        # Set color format to 16-bit RGB565
        self._write_cmd(ST7735_COLMOD)
        self._write_data([0x05])
        time.sleep(0.1)

        # Memory access control: row/col address order, RGB
        self._write_cmd(ST7735_MADCTL)
        self._write_data([0xC0])

        # Turn display on
        self._write_cmd(ST7735_DISPON)
        time.sleep(0.1)

    def _write_cmd(self, cmd):
        GPIO.output(self.dc, GPIO.LOW)
        self.spi.writebytes([cmd])

    def _write_data(self, data):
        GPIO.output(self.dc, GPIO.HIGH)
        if isinstance(data, int):
            data = [data]
        self.spi.writebytes(list(data))

    def set_window(self, x0, y0, x1, y1):

        cx = x
        for ch in text:
            self.draw_char(ch, cx, y, fg, bg, size)
            cx += 5 * size

    global _spi, _running

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _signal_handler)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _signal_handler)

    # --- SPI setup ---
    try:

        _spi.open(0, 0)  # bus 0, CE0
        _spi.max_speed_hz = 16000000
        _spi.mode = 0

    for i in range(32, 256):

        tft.draw_char(chr(i), (i - 32) % 8 * 16, (i - 32) // 8 * 16, WHITE, BLACK)
        time.sleep(0.02)

    tft.put_string("Hello,World!", 0, 0, WHITE, BLACK)
    time.sleep(3)
    if not _running:
        goto_cleanup()

    tft.put_string("TFT144", 0, 40, GREEN, BLACK, 2)
    time.sleep(3)
    if not _running:
        goto_cleanup()

    tft.fill_rect(0, 0, 128, 64, RED)
    tft.fill_rect(0, 64, 128, 64, BLACK)
    time.sleep(2)
    if not _running:
        goto_cleanup()

    # --- Draw diagonal lines ---
    print("Drawing lines...")
    tft.draw_line(0, 0, 127, 127, GREEN)
    tft.draw_line(0, 127, 127, 0, GREEN)
    time.sleep(2)

    goto_cleanup()
    return

def goto_cleanup():
    _cleanup()
    sys.exit(0)

import sys
import time

import RPi.GPIO as GPIO

TOUCH_SENSOR_PIN = 17
LED_PIN = 27
CSV_FILE = "touch_events.csv"
DEBOUNCE_MS = 300

_running = True
_csv_file = None
_csv_writer = None


def _signal_handler(signum, frame):
    global _running
    _running = False


def _init_csv():
    global _csv_file, _csv_writer
    try:
        _csv_file = open(CSV_FILE, "a", newline="")
        _csv_writer = csv.writer(_csv_file)
        if _csv_file.tell() == 0:
            _csv_writer.writerow(["Timestamp", "Event"])
            _csv_file.flush()
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f"Error initializing CSV file '{CSV_FILE}': {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        raise


def _log_event():
    timestamp = datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    try:
        _csv_writer.writerow([timestamp, "Touch Detected"])
        _csv_file.flush()
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f"Error writing to CSV file: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)

    time.sleep(DEBOUNCE_MS / 1000.0)
    if GPIO.input(channel) == GPIO.LOW:
        GPIO.output(LED_PIN, GPIO.HIGH)
        _log_event()

    global _running

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _signal_handler)

    GPIO.setup(TOUCH_SENSOR_PIN, GPIO.IN, pull_up_down=GPIO.PUD_UP)
    GPIO.setup(LED_PIN, GPIO.OUT, initial=GPIO.LOW)

    except OSError:
        GPIO.cleanup()
        sys.exit(1)

        TOUCH_SENSOR_PIN, GPIO.FALLING, callback=_touch_detected, bouncetime=DEBOUNCE_MS

        print("Program terminated.")

DATA_IN_PIN = 20

BH1750_ADDR = 0x23

# I2C bus number on Raspberry Pi (GPIO 2/SDA = bus 1, GPIO 3/SCL = bus 1)
I2C_BUS = 1

# Measurement interval in seconds
MEASUREMENT_INTERVAL = 3

# Global flag for graceful shutdown
_running = True

    """Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM for graceful shutdown."""
    global _running
    _running = False

    try:

        return None

    try:
        bus.read_byte(BH1750_ADDR)
    except OSError:

        print(f"Unexpected error: {e}")
    finally:
        bus.close()
        print("I2C bus closed. Exiting.")

# Program: Simple LED Control with Button
# Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B
# Wiring:
#   - LED anode  -> GPIO 17 (BCM, physical pin 11) via 330 Ω resistor
#   - LED cathode -> GND (physical pin 6)
#   - Button one leg -> GPIO 2 (BCM, physical pin 3)
#   - Button other leg -> GND (physical pin 6)
# The button is wired with an internal pull-up, so it reads LOW when pressed.

import signal
import sys
import time

try:
    from gpiozero import LED, Button
    from gpiozero.exc import GPIOZeroError, BadPinFactory
except ImportError:
    print("Error: gpiozero is not installed. Install with: sudo apt install python3-gpiozero")
    sys.exit(1)

# Define GPIO pins (BCM numbering)
LED_PIN = 17
BUTTON_PIN = 2

# Global references for cleanup
led = None
button = None


def signal_handler(sig, frame):
    """Handle SIGINT (Ctrl-C) to cleanly turn off the LED and release resources."""
    print("\nSIGINT received. Cleaning up...")
    if led is not None:
        led.off()
        led.close()
    if button is not None:
        button.close()
    print("GPIO cleanup complete. Exiting.")
    sys.exit(0)


def button_pressed():
    """Callback when the button is pressed (active-low -> when_pressed fires on press)."""
    led.on()
    print("LED on")


def button_released():
    """Callback when the button is released."""
    led.off()
    print("LED off")


def main():
    global led, button

    # Initialize LED and Button with error handling
    try:
        led = LED(LED_PIN)
        button = Button(BUTTON_PIN, pull_up=True)  # Internal pull-up; button reads LOW when pressed
    except BadPinFactory:
        print("Error: No GPIO pin factory available. Are you running on a Raspberry Pi?")
        sys.exit(1)
    except GPIOZeroError as e:
        print(f"Error initializing GPIO: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Unexpected error during initialization: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Verify objects are ready
    if led is None or button is None:
        print("Error: LED or button object is None.")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Attach event handlers
    button.when_pressed = button_pressed
    button.when_released = button_released

    # Register SIGINT handler
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal_handler)

    print("Program running. Press the button to turn the LED on/off. Press Ctrl-C to exit.")

    # Keep the program running indefinitely
    try:
        signal.pause()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        # Fallback if signal.pause is interrupted
        signal_handler(signal.SIGINT, None)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import signal
import threading
import time
import logging
from gpiozero import OutputDevice, InputDevice
from gpiozero.exc import GPIOZeroError, DeviceClosed

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("gpio_control")

PIN_OUTPUT = 21
PIN_TRIGGER = 20
PULSE_US = 100


class OutputPin:
    """Generic output pin with driver verification and clean shutdown."""

    def __init__(self, pin, name, initial_value=0, active_high=True):
        self.name = name
        self.pin = pin
        self.active_high = active_high
        self._value = initial_value
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._device = None
        self._closed = False
        try:
            self._device = OutputDevice(pin, active_high=active_high, initial_value=initial_value)
            log.info("OutputPin '%s' (BCM %d) initialised to %d", name, pin, initial_value)
        except GPIOZeroError as exc:
            log.error("Failed to initialise OutputPin '%s' (BCM %d): %s", name, pin, exc)
            raise

    def set_value(self, value):
        if self._closed:
            raise DeviceClosed("Cannot write to closed pin '%s'" % self.name)
        if value not in (0, 1):
            raise ValueError("OutputPin value must be 0 or 1, got %r" % value)
        with self._lock:
            self._value = value
            self._device.value = value

    def get_value(self):
        with self._lock:
            return self._value

    def shutdown(self):
        if self._closed:
            return
        with self._lock:
            if self._device is not None:
                try:
                    self._device.close()
                except Exception as exc:
                    log.warning("Error closing OutputPin '%s': %s", self.name, exc)
                finally:
                    self._device = None
            self._closed = True
            log.info("OutputPin '%s' (BCM %d) shutdown complete", self.name, self.pin)

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<OutputPin %s=%d>" % (self.name, self.get_value())


class TriggerPin(OutputPin):
    """Output pin that can emit a short high pulse (trigger)."""

    def __init__(self, pin, name, pulse_high=True, initial_value=0):
        active_high = pulse_high
        super().__init__(pin, name, initial_value=initial_value, active_high=active_high)

    def trigger(self):
        if self._closed:
            raise DeviceClosed("Cannot trigger closed pin '%s'" % self.name)
        with self._lock:
            self._value = 1
            self._device.value = 1
            time.sleep(PULSE_US / 1_000_000.0)
            self._value = 0
            self._device.value = 0
            log.info("TriggerPin '%s' (BCM %d) emitted %d us pulse", self.name, self.pin, PULSE_US)


def _make_trigger(pin, name, pulse_high=True, initial_value=0):
    return TriggerPin(pin, name, pulse_high=pulse_high, initial_value=initial_value)


def main():

    trigger = _make_trigger(PIN_TRIGGER, "ExampleTrigger", pulse_high=True, initial_value=0)

import signal
import time
import logging
import requests

try:
    from gpiozero import Button
except ImportError:
    print("gpiozero is required. Install with: sudo apt install python3-gpiozero")
    raise

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
RAIN_SENSOR_PIN = 17            # BCM numbering
ALERT_ENDPOINT = "http://example.com/alert"
DEBOUNCE_MS = 500               # 500 ms hardware debounce on the GPIO line
COOLDOWN_S = 1.0                # 1-second cooldown between alerts
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S = 10          # HTTP POST timeout

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Logging
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
)
log = logging.getLogger("rain_alert")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Graceful shutdown flag
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_running = True

def _handle_signal(signum, frame):
    global _running
    _running = False
    log.info("Signal %s received – shutting down …", signum)

signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _handle_signal)
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _handle_signal)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Alert sender
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def send_alert() -> None:
    """POST the rain-alert JSON payload, logging any network/HTTP errors."""
    payload = {"alert": "Rain detected at manufacturing line"}
    try:
        resp = requests.post(
            ALERT_ENDPOINT,
            json=payload,
            timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
        log.info("Alert sent (HTTP %s).", resp.status_code)
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
        log.error("Alert request timed out after %.0f s.", REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S)
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as exc:
        log.error("Connection error while sending alert: %s", exc)
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as exc:
        log.error("HTTP error response: %s", exc)
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
        log.error("Unexpected request error: %s", exc)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main loop
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main() -> None:
    # pull_up=True  -> internal pull-up resistor enabled.
    # bounce_time  -> ignore edges within this window (seconds).
    sensor = Button(
        RAIN_SENSOR_PIN,
        pull_up=True,
        bounce_time=DEBOUNCE_MS / 1000.0,
    )

    last_alert_time: float = 0.0

    log.info(
        "Monitoring GPIO %d for falling edges (debounce %d ms, cooldown %.1f s).",
        RAIN_SENSOR_PIN,
        DEBOUNCE_MS,
        COOLDOWN_S,
    )

    try:
        while _running:
            # wait_for_press blocks until a falling edge is detected.
            sensor.wait_for_press(timeout=0.5)

import time
import signal
import sys
import logging
import zmq

try:
    from gpiozero import PWMOutputDevice, DigitalOutputDevice
    from gpiozero.exc import GPIOZeroError, DeviceClosed
except ImportError:
    PWMOutputDevice = None
    DigitalOutputDevice = None
    GPIOZeroError = Exception
    DeviceClosed = Exception

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class PIDHandler:
    """
    PIDHandler manages error output and a ZeroMQ watchdog on a Raspberry Pi.

    It drives a PWM output on physical pin 12 (BCM GPIO 18) or a digital
    output on physical pin 10 (BCM GPIO 15) depending on the ``pwm`` flag.
    """

    def __init__(self, logger: logging.Logger, pwm: bool = True):
        self.logger = logger
        self.pwm = pwm
        self.global_err_state = False
        self.last_msg = time.time()
        self.subscribers = []
        self._shutdown = False

        self._pwm_dev = None
        self._digital_dev = None
        self._zmq_context = None
        self._zmq_socket = None

        self._init_gpio()
        self._init_zmq()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # GPIO setup
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _init_gpio(self):
        """Initialize the PWM or digital error output device."""
        if PWMOutputDevice is None or DigitalOutputDevice is None:
            self.logger.error("gpiozero is not available; cannot initialize GPIO.")
            return

        try:
            if self.pwm:
                # Physical pin 12 -> BCM GPIO 18
                self._pwm_dev = PWMOutputDevice(
                    pin=18,
                    initial_value=0.0,
                    frequency=1000,
                )
                self.logger.info("PWM error output initialized on BCM GPIO 18.")
            else:
                # Physical pin 10 -> BCM GPIO 15
                self._digital_dev = DigitalOutputDevice(
                    pin=15,
                    initial_value=False,
                )
                self.logger.info("Digital error output initialized on BCM GPIO 15.")
        except GPIOZeroError as exc:
            self.logger.error(f"Failed to initialize GPIO: {exc}")
            self._cleanup_gpio()
            raise

    def _cleanup_gpio(self):
        """Close GPIO devices if they were opened."""
        for dev in (self._pwm_dev, self._digital_dev):
            if dev is not None:
                try:
                    dev.close()
                except Exception as exc:
                    self.logger.warning(f"Error closing GPIO device: {exc}")
        self._pwm_dev = None
        self._digital_dev = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # ZeroMQ setup
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _init_zmq(self):
        """Create the ZeroMQ context and socket."""
        try:
            self._zmq_context = zmq.Context.instance()
            self._zmq_socket = self._zmq_context.socket(zmq.PULL)
            self._zmq_socket.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
            self.logger.info("ZeroMQ PULL socket initialized.")
        except zmq.ZMQError as exc:
            self.logger.error(f"Failed to initialize ZeroMQ: {exc}")
            self._cleanup_zmq()
            raise

    def _cleanup_zmq(self):
        """Close the ZeroMQ socket and terminate the context."""
        if self._zmq_socket is not None:
            try:
                self._zmq_socket.close(linger=0)
            except zmq.ZMQError as exc:
                self.logger.warning(f"Error closing ZeroMQ socket: {exc}")
            self._zmq_socket = None
        if self._zmq_context is not None:
            try:
                self._zmq_context.term()
            except zmq.ZMQError as exc:
                self.logger.warning(f"Error terminating ZeroMQ context: {exc}")
            self._zmq_context = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Error output
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def update_error_output(self):
        """Set the error output based on the global error state."""
        try:
            if self.pwm and self._pwm_dev is not None:
                self._pwm_dev.value = 1.0 if self.global_err_state else 0.0
            elif self._digital_dev is not None:
                self._digital_dev.on() if self.global_err_state else self._digital_dev.off()
        except (GPIOZeroError, DeviceClosed) as exc:
            self.logger.error(f"Failed to update error output: {exc}")

    def set_error_output(self, state: bool):
        """Directly set the error output state and update the global state."""
        self.global_err_state = state
        self.update_error_output()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Watchdog
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _check_watchdog(self):
        """Check the watchdog timeout and trigger error output if timed out."""
        if time.time() - self.last_msg > 20:
            self.logger.warning("Watchdog timeout triggered.")
            self.set_error_output(True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Message handling
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def handle_message(self):
        """Receive a message from the ZeroMQ socket and dispatch it."""
        if self._shutdown:
            return

        try:
            if self._zmq_socket is None:
                self.logger.error("ZeroMQ socket is not initialized.")
                return

            # Poll with a short timeout to allow periodic watchdog checks
            poller = zmq.Poller()
            poller.register(self._zmq_socket, zmq.POLLIN)
            events = dict(poller.poll(timeout=100))

            if self._zmq_socket in events:
                try:
                    data = self._zmq_socket.recv_string(flags=zmq.NOBLOCK)
                    self.last_msg = time.time()
                    self.logger.debug(f"Received message: {data}")
                    self._dispatch(data)
                except zmq.Again:
                    pass
                except zmq.ZMQError as exc:
                    self.logger.error(f"Error receiving message: {exc}")
            else:
                self._check_watchdog()
        except zmq.ZMQError as exc:
            self.logger.error(f"ZeroMQ error in handle_message: {exc}")
        except Exception as exc:
            self.logger.error(f"Unexpected error in handle_message: {exc}")

    def _dispatch(self, data: str):
        """Dispatch the received message to registered subscribers."""
        for subscriber in self.subscribers:
            try:
                subscriber(data)
            except Exception as exc:
                self.logger.error(f"Error in subscriber: {exc}")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Subscription
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def subscribe(self, callback):
        """Register a callback to be invoked on received messages."""
        self.subscribers.append(callback)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Cleanup
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def cleanup(self):
        """Release all resources held by the handler."""
        self._shutdown = True
        self._cleanup_zmq()
        self._cleanup_gpio()
        self.logger.info("PIDHandler cleanup complete.")

    def signal_handler(self, signum, frame):
        """Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM for graceful shutdown."""
        self.logger.info(f"Received signal {signum}; shutting down.")
        self.cleanup()
        sys.exit(0)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Example usage
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    handler = PIDHandler(logger, pwm=True)

    def example_subscriber(msg):
        print(f"Subscriber received: {msg}")

    handler.subscribe(example_subscriber)

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, handler.signal_handler)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, handler.signal_handler)

    try:
        while True:
            handler.handle_message()
            time.sleep(0.1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        handler.cleanup()

#!/usr/bin/python3
"""
OutputPin: a robust GPIO output wrapper for Raspberry Pi using the lgpio driver.

Provides full validation of pin_number (BCM 0-31) and initial_value (0 or 1),
graceful error handling when the lgpio daemon is unavailable, and a
safe shutdown that releases the driver cleanly on every exit path.
"""

import time
import logging
import signal
import sys
from typing import Optional

import lgpio

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class GPIOError(Exception):
    """Custom exception for GPIO-related errors."""
    pass


class OutputPin:
    """
    Represents a GPIO pin configured for output on a Raspberry Pi.

    Attributes:
        pin_number (int): BCM GPIO pin number (0-31).
        initial_value (int): Initial output value (0 or 1).
        _chip: lgpio.Chip instance (None if initialization failed).
    """

    def __init__(self, pin_number: int, initial_value: int) -> None:
        """
        Initialize the OutputPin.

        Args:
            pin_number: BCM GPIO pin number (0-31).
            initial_value: Initial output value (0 or 1).

        Raises:
            GPIOError: If pin_number is invalid, initial_value is invalid,
                       or the lgpio driver cannot be opened.
        """
        if not isinstance(pin_number, int) or not 0 <= pin_number <= 31:
            raise GPIOError(
                f"Invalid pin number {pin_number!r}; must be an integer in 0-31."
            )
        if initial_value not in (0, 1):
            raise GPIOError(
                f"Invalid initial value {initial_value!r}; must be 0 or 1."
            )

        self.pin_number: int = pin_number
        self.initial_value: int = initial_value
        self._chip: Optional[lgpio.Chip] = None

        try:
            self._chip = lgpio.gpiochip_open(0)
        except OSError as exc:
            raise GPIOError(
                f"Failed to open GPIO chip (lgpio daemon unavailable?): {exc}"
            ) from exc

        try:
            lgpio.gpio_claim_output(self._chip, self.pin_number, self.initial_value)
        except OSError as exc:
            self._cleanup()
            raise GPIOError(
                f"Failed to claim GPIO {self.pin_number} as output: {exc}"
            ) from exc

        logger.info(
            "Pin %d initialized as output with value %d",
            self.pin_number,
            self.initial_value,
        )

    def set_value(self, value: int) -> None:
        """
        Set the pin's output value.

        Args:
            value: New output value (0 or 1).

        Raises:
            GPIOError: If value is invalid or the driver call fails.
        """
        if value not in (0, 1):
            raise GPIOError(f"Invalid value {value!r}; must be 0 or 1.")
        if self._chip is None:
            raise GPIOError("Cannot set value: pin not initialized.")

        try:
            lgpio.gpio_write(self._chip, self.pin_number, value)
        except OSError as exc:
            raise GPIOError(f"Failed to write GPIO {self.pin_number}: {exc}") from exc

        logger.debug("Pin %d set to %d", self.pin_number, value)

    def shutdown(self) -> None:
        """
        Release the pin: claim it as input (high-impedance) and close the
        driver connection. Safe to call multiple times.
        """
        if self._chip is not None:
            try:
                lgpio.gpio_claim_input(self._chip, self.pin_number)
            except OSError as exc:
                logger.warning("Could not re-claim %d as input: %s", self.pin_number, exc)
            finally:
                self._cleanup()

    def _cleanup(self) -> None:
        """Close the lgpio chip handle."""
        if self._chip is not None:
            try:
                lgpio.gpiochip_close(self._chip)
            except OSError as exc:
                logger.warning("Error closing GPIO chip: %s", exc)
            finally:
                self._chip = None

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"OutputPin(pin_number={self.pin_number}, "
            f"initial_value={self.initial_value}, "
            f"chip={'initialized' if self._chip else 'None'})"
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_running = True


def _signal_handler(signum: int, frame) -> None:
    global _running
    logger.info("Signal %d received, shutting down...", signum)
    _running = False


def main() -> None:
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _signal_handler)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _signal_handler)

    pin: Optional[OutputPin] = None
    try:
        pin = OutputPin(pin_number=17, initial_value=0)
        logger.info("Toggling GPIO 17 every 0.5 s for 5 s...")
        start = time.monotonic()
        while _running and (time.monotonic() - start) < 5.0:
            current = 0 if pin.initial_value == 1 else 1
            pin.set_value(current)
            pin.initial_value = current
            logger.info("GPIO 17 -> %d", current)
            time.sleep(0.5)
    except GPIOError as exc:
        logger.error("GPIO error: %s", exc)
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - top-level safety net
        logger.exception("Unexpected error: %s", exc)
        sys.exit(1)
    finally:
        if pin is not None:
            pin.shutdown()
            logger.info("GPIO 17 released.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

SPI_DEVICE = 0

CE0_PIN = 8

COM_I_EN_REG = 0x02
DIV_I_EN_REG = 0x03
COM_IRQ_REG = 0x04
DIV_IRQ_REG = 0x05

TX_SEL_REG = 0x18
AUTORUN_REG = 0x22
MOD_WIDTH_REG = 0x24
RFCFG_REG = 0x26
GSR_REG = 0x2D
VERSION_REG = 0x37

CMD_IDLE = 0x00
CMD_TRANSCEIVE = 0x0C
CMD_SOFT_RESET = 0x0F

# Mode register values

MODE_TRANSCEIVE = 0x03

RESTRICTED_TAGS = ["04 11 02 13", "04 11 02 14", "04 11 02 15", "04 11 02 16"]
